Land Resources Use
At the low or projected level of development, an average of 392 acres would be disturbed annually at peak production rates (after 1989). Since approximately 7 years are required before use could be made of the land, 2,744 acres would be out of use at any given time.
At the highest possible level of development, 573 acres would be disturbed annually and a maximum of 4,011 acres would be out of use at a given time after 1989.
The land will be reclaimed and vegetative cover suitable for livestock grazing reestablished after mining. It also may have the secondary use of recreation and wildlife habitat.
The short-term loss of grazing lands due to mining will result in a ...

net loss of annual agricultural production. The loss will increase by

annual increments until it reaches approximately 100 animal units for

the low rate and 150 animal units for the high rate. It will then

stabilize or decrease depending on the degree of productivity of the

forage on the reclaimed lands. The eventual, long-term reclaimed

productivity of the mine area for grazing is unknown.
Approximately 45% of Tract II and 24% of Tract III has a medium level (3,300 board ft./acre) stand of Ponderosa pine. Mining would require removal of essentially all timber on Tract III and approximately 70% of the timber on Tract II. In all, approximately 8,630 acres of timber will be removed. The mining of the area would allow a short-term use of the timber now existing, which would offset some of the agricultural economic loss due to mining.
